body.statement:
Uniformly over fixed \(S\), every \(\lambda>0\), and all positive sample sizes, let
\[
C_{\lambda,d}:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
+\frac{d}{2\lambda+d}(\log 2)^{-2\lambda/d}.
\]
Then
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq C_{\lambda,d}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
\qquad
R_{\star,\beta}
\asymp_{\lambda,d}
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Writing
\[
a:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d},
\]
for every integer \(T\geq3\) one has
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
\qquad
R_{\star,\beta}
=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
For the independent-calendar subclass \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger,\mathrm{iid}}(\lambda)\) defined in \(\texttt{def:panel-law-class}\), and also algebraically under the separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition described in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\),
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp}}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}},
\qquad
R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Put
\[
A_\beta:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{iid}}:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}.
\]
For every fixed nonempty donor-envelope interior-compatible class \(B>D^2\), the sharp conditional minimax mean-squared-error and uniformly honest expected-length results in \(\texttt{thm:sharp-joint-frontier}\) and \(\texttt{thm:honest-length-frontier}\) imply, along their stated joint-growth arrays, rates of order
\[
A_\beta\vee N^{-\kappa}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\bigl(A_\beta\vee N^{-\kappa}\bigr)^{1/2}
\]
over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), and rates of order
\[
A_{\mathrm{iid}}\vee N^{-\kappa}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\bigl(A_{\mathrm{iid}}\vee N^{-\kappa}\bigr)^{1/2}
\]
over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger,\mathrm{iid}}(\lambda)\).  Thus, with \(A\) equal to \(A_\beta\) or \(A_{\mathrm{iid}}\) for the corresponding class, the oracle region, generated-center region, and phase boundary are respectively
\[
N^{-\kappa}=o(A),
\qquad
A=o(N^{-\kappa}),
\qquad
N\asymp A^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
At the compatible boundary \(B=D^2\), the two dependent frontier theorems retain the corresponding upper rates and exact conditional coverage but provide only their stated non-donor lower bounds; hence no sharp generated-center phase is asserted there.  If \(B<D^2\), the classes are empty and no substantive phase assertion is made.  Since
\[
R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
=\{\log(T\vee2)\}^{2\lambda/d}R_{\mathrm{sp}},
\]
conditional calendar independence removes exactly the logarithmic spacing penalty present under design-only geometric beta mixing.  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}\) removes a classical measurement-error inverse problem from the historical design, so neither frontier contains a deconvolution term or a separate moving-Gram term.  Finally, \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}\) whenever \(\lambda>1\).
body.justification: The exact diagram distinguishes a genuinely active information channel from a bookkeeping term and records higher-order saturation.
body.gap: The repeated-measurement literature has a sparse-to-dense smoothing transition, while generated-regressor and measurement-error papers imply different first-stage effects; no existing result locates this oracle boundary.
body.consumer: A study can allocate its data budget to the active axis and avoid unnecessary deconvolution when the historical paths are exact.
body.proof_tex:
Set
\[
a:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d},
\qquad
q:=\frac{2\lambda}{d}.
\]
The declared conditions \(\lambda>0\) and \(d>0\) imply \(a\in(0,1)\) and \(q>0\).  We first prove the only inequality needed for the rate reduction.  For \(u>0\), let
\[
\phi(u):=au+(1-a)-u^a.
\]
Then \(\phi(1)=0\) and
\[
\phi'(u)=a\bigl(1-u^{a-1}\bigr).
\]
Because \(a-1<0\), the derivative is negative on \((0,1)\) and positive on \((1,\infty)\).  Thus \(u=1\) is a global minimizer, so \(\phi(u)\geq0\).  Substitution of \(u=x/y\), followed by multiplication by \(y>0\), gives
\[
x^ay^{1-a}\leq ax+(1-a)y,
\qquad x>0,\qquad y>0.
\tag{1}
\]
Moreover,
\[
q(1-a)
=\frac{2\lambda}{d}\frac{d}{2\lambda+d}
=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
=a.
\tag{2}
\]
For each cohort \(s\), positivity of the integers \(T\) and \(n_s\) permits (1) to be applied with \(x=n_s^{-1}\) and \(y=T^{-q}\).  By (2),
\[
\begin{aligned}
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
&=n_s^{-a}T^{-a}\\
&=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-q})^{1-a}\\
&\leq an_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
The cohort-weight conditions in the frozen symbol declaration give \(\pi_s>0\) and \(\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s=1\).  Hence
\[
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2
\leq\left(\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\right)^2
=1.
\tag{4}
\]
Multiplying (3) by \(\pi_s^2\), summing over \(s\), applying (4), and using the definitions of \(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\) in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\), we obtain
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\tag{5}
\]

For every positive integer \(T\), one has \(\log(T\vee2)\geq\log2>0\).  Since \(q>0\), the definition of \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\) gives
\[
T^{-q}
\leq(\log2)^{-q}
\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{q}
=(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{6}
\]
Combining (5) and (6) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
&\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\\
&\leq\{a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr)\\
&=C_{\lambda,d}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Here the second line uses \(cx+dy\leq(c+d)(x\vee y)\) for nonnegative \(c,d,x,y\), and the last line uses \(1-a=d/(2\lambda+d)\) and \(q=2\lambda/d\).  Since \(0<\log2<1\) and \(q>0\),
\[
C_{\lambda,d}=a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\geq a+(1-a)=1.
\tag{8}
\]
Define
\[
A_\beta:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
\qquad
D_\beta:=A_\beta\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
All rate components are positive by \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\).  Its definition of \(R_{\star,\beta}\), together with (7)--(8), gives
\[
D_\beta
\leq R_{\star,\beta}
=D_\beta\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq D_\beta\vee(C_{\lambda,d}A_\beta)
\leq C_{\lambda,d}D_\beta.
\tag{9}
\]
This proves the asserted uniform comparison with constants \(1\) and \(C_{\lambda,d}\).

If \(T\geq3\), then \(T\vee2=T\) and \(\log T\geq\log3>1\), so
\[
T^{-q}\leq\left(\frac{\log T}{T}\right)^q
=R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{10}
\]
Substituting (10) into (5) and using \(a\in(0,1)\) gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{11}
\]
Taking the maximum with \(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\), \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\), and \(R_{\mathrm{don}}\) in the definition of \(R_{\star,\beta}\) proves
\[
R_{\star,\beta}=A_\beta\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{12}
\]

For the independent-calendar subclass in \(\texttt{def:panel-law-class}\), \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) assigns the spacing rate
\[
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2\lambda/d}=T^{-q}.
\tag{13}
\]
The same assignment applies algebraically under the separately stated fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition.  Substituting (13) directly into (5) gives, without a logarithmic relaxation,
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp}}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}.
\tag{14}
\]
Thus, with \(A_{\mathrm{iid}}:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\), the definition of \(R_\star\) yields the exact identity
\[
R_\star=A_{\mathrm{iid}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{15}
\]

We now connect (12) and (15) to the statistical experiment, rather than treating (15) as comparator algebra only.  Fix a nonempty donor-envelope interior-compatible class, so \(B>D^2\), and take a joint-growth array satisfying the limit conditions in \(\texttt{thm:sharp-joint-frontier}\) and \(\texttt{thm:honest-length-frontier}\).  The beta-mixing part of \(\texttt{thm:sharp-joint-frontier}\) identifies the conditional minimax mean-squared-error order as \(R_{\star,\beta}\), and its independent-calendar corollary identifies that order as \(R_\star\) over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger,\mathrm{iid}}(\lambda)\).  Equations (12) and (15), valid eventually because \(T\to\infty\), therefore turn these respective orders into
\[
A_\beta\vee N^{-\kappa}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
A_{\mathrm{iid}}\vee N^{-\kappa},
\tag{16}
\]
where \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}\) by \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\).  Likewise, \(\texttt{thm:honest-length-frontier}\) identifies the optimal uniformly honest expected-length orders as the square roots of the two rates, giving the two square-root expressions in the claim.

Let \(A\) denote either positive quantity \(A_\beta\) or \(A_{\mathrm{iid}}\), as appropriate.  In (16), the donor term is asymptotically negligible precisely when
\[
N^{-\kappa}=o(A),
\tag{17}
\]
and is asymptotically dominant precisely when
\[
A=o(N^{-\kappa}).
\tag{18}
\]
Taking square roots preserves both little-order comparisons, so the same regions govern the honest-length rates.  Since \(A>0\) and \(\kappa>0\), the boundary relation \(N^{-\kappa}\asymp A\) is equivalent, after applying the decreasing map \(x\mapsto x^{-1/\kappa}\) and absorbing fixed comparison constants, to
\[
N\asymp A^{-1/\kappa}.
\tag{19}
\]
This proves both phase diagrams.

At \(B=D^2\), the boundary clauses of \(\texttt{thm:sharp-joint-frontier}\) and \(\texttt{thm:honest-length-frontier}\) retain the displayed upper rates and exact conditional coverage but lower-bound only the respective non-donor channel maxima.  Hence (17)--(19) cannot be promoted to a sharp donor phase at equality.  The same theorems state that \(B<D^2\) gives an empty class, so no minimax phase is asserted there.  These case distinctions use exactly the compatibility and limit conditions of the dependent statistical results.

Finally, the two spacing definitions give the exact ratio
\[
\frac{R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}}{R_{\mathrm{sp}}}
=\{\log(T\vee2)\}^{2\lambda/d},
\tag{20}
\]
which proves the stated dependence elbow: the independent-calendar subclass removes the logarithmic factor and changes no other active channel.  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}\) states
\[
X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}.
\tag{21}
\]
Thus the historical regression coordinate is observed without a measurement-error convolution, so no inversion of such a convolution is required.  Inspection of the exhaustive maxima defining \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and \(R_\star\) in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) then shows that neither contains a deconvolution component or a separate moving-Gram component.  The same definition sets \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).  If \(\lambda>1\), then \(\kappa=1\), and consequently
\[
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}=N^{-1}.
\]
All assertions follow.
